answer: An attacker who floods the jury with fake votes also floods itself with the cost of its own dishonest votes, because every vote is penalized when it backs a bad answer. The defense holds because trust accrues slowly and is lost fast, so a farm that ever submits a copied answer destroys the value of that identity. What this achieves is a system where the cost of an attack is public and provable, so the whole network can trust verdicts without trusting any single identity.
